summary: The starter prompt plus the provided skill.md give a clear, implementable request: a Node.js (Mongoose) cart service that uses DocumentDB multi-document transactions, optimistic locking via a version field, and clear out-of-stock errors. Several important implementation details (Mongoose/driver versions, exact API endpoints and error format, test harness and seed-script conventions, and index choices) are unspecified and will be decided by the builder’s defaults or require author clarification.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js cart service using Mongoose that stores cart and inventory documents in DocumentDB. Use multi-document transactions to atomically decrement stock and add items to the cart. Handle optimistic locking with a version field and surface clear errors when stock is exhausted."
rubric.note: Business problem, user and behavior (atomic add-to-cart with inventory protection) are explicitly stated.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js cart service" (single service implementation implied)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement a single-agent application (one Node.js service) providing an API for cart operations (no multi-agent/orchestration framework).
rubric.note: Prompt implies a single application (no multi-agent coordination).

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use Node.js runtime available on the run environment; skill.md specifies Node.js 24 is available, so builder will target Node.js 24.
rubric.note: Language is explicit; Node.js version is provided by skill.md (Node.js 24).

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will pick a recent, Node-24-compatible Mongoose major (likely Mongoose 7.x). MongoDB driver compatibility will follow whatever Mongoose depends on.
rubric.note: Prompt names Mongoose but does not fix a version. A concrete version should be decided (or left to latest stable) for reproducibility.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the live DocumentDB cluster described in skill.md (M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol) and the database sample_retail_05.
rubric.note: The run-environment (cluster tier and database name) is given in skill.md.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Connection string will be read at runtime from DOCUMENTDB_URI (per skill.md). Do not commit secrets; provide .env.example with placeholders.
rubric.note: skill.md explicitly instructs to read DOCUMENTDB_URI from env and not to write it to files.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "stores cart and inventory documents" and "version field" and "cart and inventory documents"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Inventory schema will include numeric stock and numeric version; Cart schema will have userId and items array with productId and quantity, stored in sample_retail_05.
rubric.note: Prompt explicitly requires Inventory stock + version and Cart with userId and items.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create a small hand-authored seed dataset (a few products and one cart) for demo purposes unless instructed otherwise.
rubric.note: Prompt and skill.md require verifying against live cluster but do not specify a seed script, data source, size, or licensing.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create minimal indexes needed for the demonstrated queries (e.g., index on productId in inventory and userId in cart) but specifics (compound/vector/TTL) are not provided and will be chosen ad-hoc.
rubric.note: No index definitions or explicit query patterns are provided; vector/index specifics in skill.md are irrelevant to this transactional cart sample unless a vector search is added.
No AI/embedding/chat components are part of the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js cart service using Mongoose"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will expose an HTTP JSON API (likely Express) with endpoints such as POST /cart/:userId/add or POST /cart/add that accept productId and quantity. CLI or UI is not specified.
rubric.note: Prompt does not specify routes, input payloads, or response shape; most builders will implement a small REST API.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision a new cluster; use the existing DocumentDB cluster described in skill.md. If deployment code is included, it should not create a cluster unless run-policy allows Azure writes.
rubric.note: skill.md explicitly states a cluster is already provisioned and to avoid provisioning another unless allowed.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add README with basic npm install / npm run seed / npm test commands, but exact test commands and expectations are unspecified.
rubric.note: Prompt asks to use transactions and handle conflicts but doesn't require test scripts or describe how to run them; reference requires integration concurrency test which is not specified here.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat successful demo runs that show atomicity, correct optimistic-lock retries, and no oversell as done; exact acceptance criteria (tests pass, README present) are not defined in the prompt.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance checklist is provided.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will avoid production-hardening (e.g., full HA, CMK) unless explicitly asked; cost and region constraints are not specified.
rubric.note: Prompt does not state cost limits, scale targets, or things to exclude.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Follow the run-environment guidance: use sample_retail_05 DB, read DOCUMENTDB_URI from env, provide a .env.example with placeholders, and do not commit secrets.
rubric.note: skill.md defines several repo/run conventions (env var, DB name, don't commit secrets).

questions_for_author: What API endpoints and request/response shapes do you want? (e.g., POST /cart/:userId/add with { productId, quantity } and what error format/code for out-of-stock and conflict?)
What retry policy should the sample use for optimistic-lock conflicts (how many retries, backoff strategy) or should it return a conflict after a single failure?
Do you require the integration concurrency simulation (parallel add-to-cart) and an automated test that runs against the live cluster, or would a local/unit-level concurrency test be acceptable?
requirements_at_risk: Include an automated integration test or concurrency simulation that issues parallel add-to-cart requests and asserts no overselling — the prompt asks to handle optimistic locking but does not require or describe such an integration test; absent explicit instruction, builder may omit or implement only manual checks.

Seed script loads sample data and creates the index and can be run twice without duplicating data — prompt/skill.md ask to verify against the live cluster but do not prescribe an idempotent seed script.

One database client is created and reused across requests — the prompt does not mention client lifecycle; although a driver best-practices skill exists, without explicit instruction the builder may instantiate per-request.

Queries and index shapes (including any vector/full-text indexes and parameters) — prompt gives no index definitions; indexing choices needed for performance and demonstration are likely to be chosen ad-hoc or omitted.

Dependencies pinned in a requirements file — the prompt doesn't require pinned dependency files (and the reference's mention of requirements.txt is Python-centric), so reproducible pinning may be missing.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — prompt does not require offline unit tests or mock strategy; builder may only provide tests that require a live DocumentDB instance.

Infrastructure-as-code for the cluster — prompt/skill.md state a cluster already exists and do not instruct to provide Bicep/Terraform for it; reference requires infra code which is likely to be absent.
README covers prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — the prompt doesn't mandate README content; the builder may include a minimal README but the full required sections are at risk.

Sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout and no former or neighbouring product name — neither the prompt nor skill.md explicitly instruct naming conventions for documentation, so inconsistent naming is possible.
